headline: Savannah Historic District and Fort Permits
reservation: Entry to the historic district is open, but guided house museum tours and boutique inns require reservations months in advance for spring azalea season. Fort Pulaski National Monument requires a per-person entrance fee; check the official National Park Service site for current pass requirements and weapons demonstration schedules.

days.title: Historic Squares and Riverfront

stops.name: Forsyth Park
stops.detail: View the iconic fountain and walk under the canopy of moss-draped live oaks.

stops.name: River Street
stops.detail: Stroll the cobblestone waterfront to see large cargo ships navigating the Savannah River.

days.driving: Walking is recommended; local transfers available for distant squares.
days.note: Cobblestones near the riverfront are uneven; pace your walk accordingly.

days.title: Coastal Forts and Barrier Islands
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Historic District

stops.name: Fort Pulaski National Monument
stops.detail: Explore the 19th-century masonry fortification and its surrounding dike system trails.

stops.name: Tybee Island Lighthouse
stops.detail: Climb Georgia's oldest and tallest lighthouse for panoramic views of the Atlantic coast.

days.driving: Allow 30–50 minutes to Tybee Island; traffic varies by season.
days.note: Lighthouse hours are seasonal and may be affected by weather conditions.

days.title: Lowcountry Wildlife and Marshes

stops.name: Savannah National Wildlife Refuge
stops.detail: Drive the wildlife loop to spot alligators and migratory water birds in former rice fields.

stops.name: Skidaway Island State Park
stops.detail: Hike the Big Ferry Trail through maritime forests and past coastal salt marshes.

days.driving: Allow 25–40 minutes between sites; conditions vary.
days.note: Check the refuge website for seasonal closures of the wildlife drive.

intel.title: Historic District Meters
intel.text: Street parking in the historic core is metered and highly regulated; use city-operated garages for longer stays. Many squares have specific loading zones that must be avoided.

intel.title: Refuge Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is weak within the Savannah National Wildlife Refuge interior. Ensure you have physical maps or downloaded data before starting the wildlife drive.

intel.title: Island Logistics
intel.text: Fuel is readily available in Savannah and on Tybee Island, but sparse along the marsh causeways. Fill your tank before heading to more remote parts of Skidaway Island.

intel.title: Tide Awareness
intel.text: Check tide charts if planning to walk the Tybee sandbars, as incoming tides can move quickly. Some marsh trails may experience flooding during extreme high tides.

intel.title: Bridge Openings
intel.text: The Talmadge Memorial Bridge is a high-span, but smaller coastal bridges may have delays. Check for local marine traffic advisories if traveling to nearby sea islands.

plan.arrival: Collect your rental at SAV and drive 20 minutes to the Historic District. Supply runs are best done in the mid-city area before entering the narrow historic streets.
plan.vehicle: Small to mid-size cars are ideal for navigating narrow historic streets; check parking garage height limits if driving a larger RV.
plan.goldenHour: Tybee Island North Beach offers a vantage point for watching ships pass during the soft evening light.
